decisions.why: FR-002 names 0277, 412 and 414 this way. 0265 is a pointer for one sub-item of Q2, and D1(2) and D2(2) still list rents by metal ('rents (0265, both ways)'), so the reply still answers rents; nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: Legal rates 1609/1700/1842 and setters, enforcement from the orders, a prosecution SILENT, the market's straying by period, the fixed-by-count ladder and its effect on weighed silver, the changers' resistance to the nanryo.
decisions.why: Carries every part of Q1 for Japan. The flat 'a prosecution SILENT' is a reported result of the pass already made (Summary: written from passes/japan.md), carried as still open per FR-001, not a narrowing of the question.

decisions.id: D1(2) Japan who priced and paid
decisions.summary: Pattern by transaction kind and region, wages, rents (0265), taxes, stipends through the fudasashi, shop purchases in copper; fees attested and the uncited 1-2% said to be uncited.
decisions.why: Every transaction kind the issue lists, and the changers' fees, appear.

decisions.summary: Edo 1842 copper-only cuts, Tsugaru coin and note prices, Edo 1854-68 values for one face, Tenpo coin at about 80, premia for old coin, Sengoku bad coin, a gold-payment premium searched (SILENT with the search if none); how fast copper prices followed the rate outside 1842 SILENT.
decisions.why: Carries Q3. The flat SILENT on copper prices outside 1842 rests on the premise that the Japan pass looked and found nothing (Summary); it is a finding carried as open under FR-001, not a refusal to answer. The record's reply must say so; if the pass did not in fact search (414's Japanese series, if any, included), that premise fails and this becomes a narrowing.

decisions.id: D1(4) Japan winners and losers - episodes and figures
decisions.summary: Q4 for Japan covers 'the four groups ... the recoinage gains, the 1860s silver-west real wage, and what people did'; the Meiwa iron and brass coins and the Tenpo episode, which the request names, and any Japanese tax-burden figure are not named, and no SILENT is recorded for them.
decisions.why: The request's Q4 names the episodes ('the Meiwa iron and brass coins; Tenpo; ...') and asks for 'the size of the effect on a laborer's real wage and a tax burden in named episodes'. 'Meiwa' appears in no block; Tenpo appears only under D1(3) as a price item; the one real-wage episode D1(4) names (the 1860s) is not one the request named, and no Japanese tax-burden effect is named. Everywhere else the plan records silence explicitly, so an unrecorded omission reads as a drop, not a finding. Not impossible, not implied by the request, not purpose-defeating. D1(4) should name the Meiwa and Tenpo episodes (and any recoinage it measures), each with its real-wage and tax-burden effect where the sources give it or SILENT with the search.

decisions.id: D1/D2 canon line - Q3's canon omitted
decisions.summary: D1 sets the answers against 'Rokugan's fixed decimal coinage and the money skill's who uses which coin'; D2 'as D1'. Q3's canon - the conversion table that converts each coin through its era's rate into silver, then by the basket - is not named.
decisions.why: FR-003: each answer is set against ITS question's canon, and the request gives Q3 its own canon with the consequence spelled out ('if copper prices were sticky, a mon amount should be measured against copper prices instead'). The plan names Q1's and Q2's canons only, so the Q3 answer - the one with a direct consequence for the conversion table - is set against nothing. Not impossible, not implied, not purpose-defeating. D1's canon line (and D2's by reference) should name the conversion table for Q3, and Q4 as having no canon yet, as the request states.

decisions.summary: Qing first and Ming where found; legal rates, bans, drift, Xianfeng notes and big cash, Ming paper; silver for tax and trade, copper for retail and labor, banks' spreads dated late Qing, retail cash shop's fee SILENT; sticky copper prices and payment-dependent prices, gold payment searched; taxpayers, officials, state, soldiers, merchants and wage earners on 414's inference only, said so.
decisions.why: Matches 'Qing (and Ming where found)' and carries each of the four questions with the named Qing crisis (Zeng Guofan's doubling for the tax burden). The flat SILENT on the cash shop's fee is a reported pass result carried as open; dating Morse as late Qing and labeling 414's inference are honesty, not narrowing. Searching gold payment in China is extra reach, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: implementation-check.md holds each new question's line.
decisions.why: FR-004 as written.

decisions.summary: Comment on #16: per figure the fragment file, verdict and what is open; per question the canon standing and any escalation.
decisions.why: FR-001, FR-003, FR-005 as written.

decisions.summary: Page sessions, implementation check, reply and landing.

decisions.summary: 0277's legal rates and market series, 412's coin questions, 414's copper wages and 0265's rents are named, not repeated; unreadable PDFs fetched with curl and read with pdftotext, images to the checks.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires 0277, 412 and 414 named, not repeated; the request itself says the record already holds 0277's rates and asks for the working of the system beyond them. Reading method is procedure, not scope.

decisions.summary: XII research: physical tasks with five boxes; XIII record checks green; XVI built as the spec's FRs.
decisions.why: Process conformance only; decides no scope.

decisions.summary: Japan's legal rates (1609, 1700, 1842), who set them, enforcement as the orders print it, prosecution SILENT; market straying by period; fixed-by-count ladder and its effect on weighed silver; changers' resistance to the nanryo.
decisions.why: Carries every clause of question 1: legal rate, who set it, enforcement, how far and long the market strayed, fixed-by-count against floating. A SILENT verdict on prosecution reports a gap; it does not narrow what is searched.

decisions.summary: Pattern by transaction kind and region (wholesale/retail, east gold/west silver, wages, rents, taxes, stipends via fudasashi, shop purchases in copper) and the attested fees, the uncited 1-2% flagged as uncited.
decisions.why: Walks every transaction kind the request lists and the changers' fees; flagging an uncited figure is the citation rule, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Dual prices by coin (Edo 1842, Tsugaru coin/note, Edo 1854-68 face values, Tenpo coin at about 80, premia for old coin, Sengoku bad coin), a gold-payment premium searched and SILENT if none; speed of copper prices following the rate outside 1842 SILENT, the Japan pass having searched and 414's series being in silver.
decisions.why: Question 3's examples-with-dates and the debased-coin premium/discount are carried; the follow-speed figure is searched and reported as open (FR-001 'what is still open'), with the reason 414 cannot supply it stated. Reporting an unfound figure as SILENT after a search does not narrow the request.

decisions.summary: The four groups the issue names across the Meiwa iron and brass coins (1769-1778, about 4,000 to 6,000 mon), the Tenpo recoinage and copper's 1830s-40s fall, the Bunsei/Tenpo/Man'en recoinage gains and the 1860s silver-west real wage; per episode the real-wage and tax-burden effect where a source gives one, SILENT with the search where none; what people did.
decisions.why: Round 1's finding is cured: both episodes the request names for Japan (Meiwa, Tenpo) are now carried with the requested real-wage and tax-burden measures, plus recoinage episodes the request's 'or a recoinage changed a metal's content' covers; SILENT-with-search is reporting, not narrowing.

decisions.summary: Each question set against its own canon: Q1 Rokugan's fixed decimal coinage; Q2 the skill's 'Coins and who uses them'; Q3 the conversion table and the request's sticky-copper consequence; Q4 none yet; stated as material for the GM, contradictions escalated.
decisions.why: Round 1's finding is cured: the canon line now matches the request's 'Canon beside it' line per question verbatim in substance, and FR-003's escalation is kept.

decisions.summary: Qing legal rates (1645, 1653), the 1684 ban, 1702 old-coin discount, 1737 brokers and treasury releases, drift to about 2,000 by 1837; Xianfeng notes and big cash; Ming paper's legal rate, gold 1:4, its fall, the bans and their lifting.
decisions.why: Carries the request's Qing-and-Ming-where-found scope for legal rate, enforcement and market straying.

decisions.summary: Silver for tax, salt levies, official pay, long-distance trade; copper for retail, salt, labor, materials; the 1436 commutation and Single Whip; tael standards and banks' spreads (Morse, late Qing, dated as such); rents (0265); a retail cash shop's fee SILENT.
decisions.why: Pattern by transaction kind and changers' spreads as a figure are carried; dating Morse as late Qing and marking a gap SILENT are honesty about coverage, not narrowing.

decisions.summary: Sticky copper prices (salt 1728, rice about 1850, wages from 414) and the dissent; payment-dependent prices in Xianfeng Beijing; light coin at 70%; paying in gold, the Qing case searched, SILENT if none.
decisions.why: Carries both halves of question 3 (price by coin; whether copper prices stuck) for China.

decisions.summary: Taxpayers (Zeng Guofan's doubling; Henan 1905), officials, the state's arrears, soldiers; merchants and wage earners from 414's inference only, said so.
decisions.why: The Qing silver-dear crisis the request names is the frame; tax-burden figures are given and the wage-earner effect is reported with its evidentiary limit stated rather than dropped. Samurai stipends have no Qing analogue; officials and soldiers on pay stand in their place.

decisions.summary: Each question against its canon as D1, question 3's conversion table included, Qing sticky copper while silver doubled named as the request's case.
decisions.why: Same per-question canon as the request gives; cures round 1's finding for D2.

blocks: ## T01 - question A, Japan's three monies (D1)
## T02 - question B, China's silver and copper (D2)

decisions.summary: T01 answers the four questions of #16 for Edo Japan, in order, each set against its canon; the canon (l7r.md 'Money') is read, not edited.
decisions.why: The issue asks Japan first with all four questions, and says the research is so the GM 'can decide how much of that to import'; leaving the canon unedited leaves that decision with the GM, as FR-003 requires.

decisions.summary: A changer's fee computed from a rate is labeled this project's arithmetic; a reading only one source gives (Kano's fee, Iwahashi's premium) is set beside the other reading.
decisions.why: Labeling, under the record's citation rules. Q2 asks for the changers' fees as a percentage and Q3 for premiums; neither is dropped.

decisions.summary: Where no source answers (a premium for paying in gold; a prosecution under the legal rate; a Meiwa-An'ei real wage in copper; a measured tax burden) the answer is SILENT with the search, not a borrowed figure.
decisions.why: Every sub-question is still searched and reported, and the exit applies only where the search finds no source. The issue asks what 'the actual reality was'. A borrowed figure would misstate that, and the accepted reply on #16 already says Q4 is 'measured where the sources allow'. No question or figure is dropped from scope.

decisions.summary: Write (s1), check and apply (s3), round-3 tail closed by the arbiter (ask:416-round4), then the marks (s4); done is record-owed clean for 0295 and money-candidates CHECK=1.
decisions.why: Process and the record's checks (FR-002). The scope of what is answered does not change.

decisions.summary: The same four answers for Ming and Qing China: legal cash rates and enforcement, Xianfeng notes and big cash, Ming paper; silver for tax and trade against copper for retail and wages; sticky copper prices; who won and lost in the silver crisis.
decisions.why: The issue asks for Qing, and Ming where found, beside Japan. Q4 names the Qing 'silver dear, copper cheap' crisis and recoinages that changed a metal's content (the Xianfeng big cash is one), and the accepted reply named Ming paper money. Nothing is added beyond those.

decisions.summary: A late-Qing standard (Morse) is dated as such; a second-hand report is labeled ATTESTED ONLY FOR; SILENT with the search for paying in gold under the Qing, a retail cash shop's fee and a measured real wage; the wage earners' case is said to be feature 414's inference.
decisions.why: Each one is provenance labeling, or an honest exit after a search. No question is removed, and the inference is labeled as an inference rather than presented as a measurement.

decisions.summary: Each new question gets its line in implementation-check.md; make impl-check F=416 reports nothing missing; no code decides a coin's worth.
decisions.why: This is FR-004, a project rule for research features. It adds no behavior and narrows nothing in the request.

decisions.summary: The reply on #16 gives every figure its fragment file, verdict and what is open; each answer stands against its canon; GM items go through escalation-check first.
decisions.why: FR-001, FR-003 and FR-005, which carry the issue's 'Figure needed' and 'Canon beside it' lines. The escalation route is a project rule and does not narrow the request.

decisions.summary: Write the feature report and land.
decisions.why: Closing steps of the workflow, with no decision about scope.
